w: Founded in 670 CE by the Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi at the city's founding, this is among the oldest places of worship in the Islamic world and the model for later Maghreb mosques. Its arches were the first known Islamic use of the horseshoe form. Aghlabid rebuilding two centuries later gave it its present shape.
s: One of the oldest mosques in the Islamic world

w: Built around 1683 by the Muradid ruler Mohamed Bey for Kairouan's Hanafi Muslim community, during a succession conflict with his brother Ali Bey. It stands within the medina of Kairouan, a mosque raised to serve one Islamic legal school rather than the whole population.
s: Built by one brother for one sect, amid a succession feud

w: Ten kilometres from Kairouan, Raqqada was built as the Aghlabid dynasty's second capital in the 9th century, a purpose-built seat of power away from the older holy city. Little of the original palace complex remains standing, but the site today houses the National Museum of Islamic Art.
s: A 9th-century Aghlabid capital, now a museum site
_facts: second capital of the 9th-century Aghlabid dynasty

w: Commissioned in 866 by a private local patron, Muhammad ibn Khairun, this small Aghlabid-era mosque carries one of the earliest richly decorated facades in Islamic architecture, three carved doorways facing the street. Its minaret was added later, in 1440, under Hafsid rule.
s: One of Islamic architecture's earliest decorated facades
_facts: commissioned in 866 by Muhammad ibn Khairun, a private patron

w: Built between 946 and 972 as a walled Fatimid capital near Kairouan, Sabra al-Mansuriya held palaces set among gardens, pools and water channels. It briefly governed a state stretching across North Africa and Sicily, then was destroyed by the Banu Hilal in 1057; only faint traces remain today.
s: A lost Fatimid capital of palaces and pleasure gardens

w: A Jewish congregation and synagogue in Kairouan that operated from 1920 until the 1970s, a marker of the city's once-established Jewish community in a town otherwise defined by its status as a holy city of Islam.
s: A synagogue that served Kairouan's Jewish community
